thread:
Mike G: RFC follow-up — tenant-edge route eviction + failover plan. Proposal: prefer ephemeral per-tenant endpoints with regional affinity, evict idle bindings aggressively, and add a short "grace" overlay to avoid blackholing active KV-cache backed sessions. looking for architecture + ops take. TL;DR below.
Sara L: Question: how do we define "idle" without dropping in-flight long-polling clients? we have some streams that are quiet for >30s but still active.
Dan K: Agree — need session heuristics. Maybe base eviction on active kv-cache refs + recent seq activity. If no KV touch for X secs, eligible.
Jess P: Also watch SNAT/table exhaustion if we push everyone to a handful of regional shared endpoints as fallback. that was a pain last quarter.
Mike G: Good points. Proposal specifics: 1) eviction_secs default 60s for ephemeral endpoints, configurable per-customer; 2) grace_window 180s — when evicted, routes go to overlay with sticky mapping for that grace period to avoid in-flight cold misses; 3) fallback_policy: regional-shared endpoint w/ source address preservation where possible.
Sara L: Grace overlay sounds promising. Are we talking about routing-level NAT preservation or TLS SNI preservation?
Dan K: Ideally both. For quick wins we can preserve source IP via x-forwarded-for + SNAT pinning where cloud provider allows. For certs we need SNI passthrough or short-lived leaf certs — heavier.
Jess P: Suggest starting with SNAT pinning + session pinhole in the edge LB, then iterate on SNI. That avoids a big cert rollout.
Mike G: Implementation sketch: on eviction, mark route state EVACUATING and install 2 rules: (a) traffic matching kv-cache token -> continue to ephemeral host for grace_window; (b) everything else -> regional-shared fallback. After grace_window, remove ephemeral host binding.
Dan K: Can we implement rule (a) as a dynamic ACL keyed by token hash? performance-wise should be fine if we use consistent hashing and small bloom filter.
Jess P: We should also limit eviction churn — add hysteresis. e.g., only evict if idle for >eviction_secs AND age > min_binding_age (default 5m). avoids oscillation on noisy workloads.
Mike G: Good call. Add min_binding_age to opt. Also we should add a metric: eviction_repromote_count to track churn and alert.
Sara L: What about control plane separation concerns? If control plane is in a different VPC/account, can we rely on synchronous writes to propagate route state in time for fast failover?
Mike G: We should assume eventual consistency. Plan: local dataplane should have a small authoritative cache for route states (TTL ~30s) that can be updated via async stream from control plane. For critical handoffs we can emit a direct push RPC to the edge relay as a best-effort fast-path.
Dan K: That implies we need an idempotent push API and replay window. Also auth — cross-account tokens short-lived.
Jess P: ops-side: for Dedicated customers with strict networking we might allow a customer-managed fallback endpoint (vpc endpoint) instead of our regional-shared NAT. config flag: fallback.type = [redwood_shared, customer_endpoint].
Mike G: Nice. That solves SNAT worries. We'll need onboarding docs and a validation step in the installer.
infra-bot: deployment scheduled: canary rollout to us-west-2 edge pool on Monday 03:00 UTC. See runbook: https://go/infra/runbooks/route-eviction-canary
Sara L: Can we gate canary on these metrics: 1) connection_reset_rate <= baseline + 0.5%; 2) eviction_repromote_count < 5 per minute per edge; 3) 99th p99 latency change < 10ms?
Mike G: Yes. Add healthcheck hooks to the canary pipeline. Also add rollback if SNAT utilization > 80% on the fallback pools.
Dan K: One more: cost tradeoff — ephemeral endpoints per tenant increase ENI count and LB rules. fallback to shared reduces costs but risks SNAT exhaustion. Need to include expected cost delta per 10k tenants in RFC appendix.
Mike G: I'll add a quick cost model. action items: Mike -> add min_binding_age + hysteresis + metrics; Sara -> spec grace overlay and token pinning; Dan -> design push API and auth; Jess -> runbook updates + fallback endpoint opt-in flow. Can we sync Wed 14:00 for final sign-off?
Sara L: Wed 14:00 works. I'll draft the grace overlay sketch before then. :+1:
Dan K: ok. I'll prototype the push-api by EOD Fri.
Jess P: I'll update runbook and test SNAT counters on staging.
Mike G: Great. Thanks team. I'll update the RFC doc with these decisions and the canary gates.
